title: 1990 Air Force low-voltage vacuum test of Biefeld-Brown

tellings.quote: For example, in 1990, the Air Force tested a Biefeld-Brown experiment in a vacuum, but they only used 19 kilovolts instead of the megavoltage Brown was using.

plain: In 1990, the Air Force tested the Biefeld-Brown effect, a claimed push produced by charging a device to very high voltage and named in part for the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown. According to Jesse Michels, the test was run in a vacuum at only 19 kilovolts, far below the millions of volts Brown himself used. Michels tells this himself, without naming a source, in a documentary about Brown, and his point is that the test never fairly reproduced Brown's work.
